name: Nazy's Guest House
imgAlt: Village of Jokolo in the Pankisi Valley
text: Widely described as the most established guesthouse in the valley. Home-cooked Georgian and Kist meals, and the hosts can arrange walking tours, horse riding, bike hire and camping gear. Food tours and cooking experiences are also arranged through the house.

name: Melissa's Guest House
text: A guesthouse in Duisi, the valley's main village. It is also known as the place that hosts the Wednesday Hadjist Zikr, a Sufi devotional ceremony. Ask before visiting; it is a religious gathering, not a show.

name: Cafe Pankisi
text: One of the few standalone cafes in the valley, serving Kisturi beer, the local non-alcoholic brew. Most other meals in Pankisi are eaten at guesthouses, served on request, so book ahead.

name: Kisturi Beer Brewery
text: A small brewery run by Shengeli Toxosashvili, offering tastings and tours of Kisturi Ludi, a tangy, kombucha-like drink made from highland fruits and wild herbs such as rosehip and black hawthorn.

name: Dinner at a Kist home
text: The authentic way to eat in Pankisi: a family table with pumpkin-filled flatbreads, noodles with mutton, fresh cheese, hand-churned butter and stone-ground maize bread. Arrange it through your guesthouse.

name: Old Mosque (1902)
text: The valley's first mosque, built in 1902 and still in use. Women's zikr takes place here on Friday mornings. Dress modestly and ask before entering.

name: New Mosque (2002)
text: Completed in 2002 on the main road, in red brick with a traditional minaret.

name: St George's Church
text: Consecrated in 1888 and no longer in regular use, but looked after by local Kists. Ask at your guesthouse for the key.

name: Old Kist cemetery
text: The oldest burial ground in the valley, with 19th-century gravestones inscribed in Arabic and Georgian, reaching back to the first Chechen settlers.

name: Pankisi Ethnographic Museum
text: Traditional instruments, carpets, feltwork and antiques. Visits are by appointment, and a local guide is recommended.

name: Duisi Watchtower
text: A stone tower above the village, reached by a marked path from the main road.

name: Amphitheatre & WWII memorial
text: Built in 1985 on the ridge above Duisi. It hosts community events, including the spring Pankisoba festival.

name: Heritage timber houses
text: Traditional Kakhetian homes with carved wooden balconies and lattice work, on the east bank at Omalo and at the north-west end near Dzibakhevi.

name: Batsara Nature Reserve
text: Home to one of the largest old yew groves in the world. Visits are arranged through the Agency of Protected Areas.

name: Tbatana plateau
imgAlt: Pankisi and the Alazani plain seen from Tbatani
text: A mountain plateau with views of the Greater Caucasus, reachable by bike, 4WD or horse. Shepherd huts are occupied from June to September.

name: Khadori Waterfall
text: A cascade down a rock wall with a pool at the base, at the northern end of the valley beyond Birkiani.

name: Pankisi Fortress trail
text: A 4.6 km circular route of about 2.5 hours, starting in Khalatsani.

name: Duisi Panorama
imgAlt: Upper part of the Pankisi valley
text: An easy hill walk above Duisi, popular at sunset.

name: Alazani River
text: Rocky riverside paths for walking and cycling; when the water is high, fishing, kayaking and tyre-rafting.

name: Zelimkhan, mountain bike tours
text: A local operator running guided mountain bike tours in the valley and foothills.

name: Pankisi Adventure Treks
text: Horse trekking from short rides to multi-day trips into the mountains.

name: Zizi's felt-making studio
text: A home studio and gift shop where you can watch felt being made by hand.

name: Duisi Community Center
text: Teaches local children feltwork and clay pottery.

name: Akhmeta (gateway town)
text: The municipal centre south of the valley, where shops, banks and onward transport are found. Most visitors pass through here on the way to Pankisi.
